intended_object: The canonical B-linear isomorphism between the tangent space at the identity of the affine group scheme Spec A and the derivations at the counit point. The tangent space is the kernel of the reduction from dual-number points A → B[ε] to B-points; the derivations are Der_R(A, B), with B acting on A through the counit. Inferred from the docstrings of this definition, of tangentKer and of derivationMulEquivTangentKer.
explanation: The underlying bijection is derivationMulEquivTangentKer. It sends a derivation d to the dual-number algebra map a ↦ ε(a) + d(a)ε, built with derivationToDualNumberEquivLift. It is shown to land in the kernel of the dual-number reduction and to turn convolution into addition of derivations, so it is the classical identification of first-order points over the identity with derivations at the counit. The B-module structure on Additive (tangentKer R A B) is defined by carrying over the structure on derivations along this same equivalence, so packaging it as a ≃ₗ[B] is the standard way to give the tangent space its linear structure and B-linearity holds automatically. The setting (a commutative Hopf algebra over a commutative semiring, with an arbitrary commutative R-algebra B) is the natural one: the antipode is needed for the convolution group in which tangentKer is a subgroup. I did not search Mathlib for a counterpart; to my knowledge it has none for this Hopf-algebra statement. derivationToSquareZeroEquivLift is related but is not the same object.
